intended_object: The ideal of the coordinate Hopf algebra of the unitriangular group scheme U_n over a commutative ring K that is generated by the coordinates x_{ij} with 0 < j − i < r. It cuts out the closed subgroup F_r of unitriangular matrices whose superdiagonals 1, …, r−1 vanish, i.e. the r-th stage of the standard superdiagonal (lower central) filtration. This is inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and `mem_stage_iff`.
explanation:
The body is `Ideal.span` of the images x_{ij} of the universal matrix entries in the unitriangular coordinate ring, for i < j and j < i + r. That is exactly the set of strict upper entries lying below the r-th superdiagonal, as the docstring says.

The library's `mem_stage_iff` shows that a K-algebra map f : O(U_n) → R kills this ideal exactly when the corresponding R-point lies in `superdiagonalSubgroup n R r`. That subgroup is {g : (g − 1)_{ij} = 0 whenever j < i + r}. So the ideal is the defining ideal of the closed subgroup scheme F_r.

The degenerate cases are right:
- r = 0 and r = 1 give the zero ideal, since F_0 = F_1 = U_n.
- r ≥ n gives all strict upper entries, so the quotient is the coordinate ring of the trivial group.

On generality: the base K is an arbitrary commutative ring, which is the natural setting for a Hopf ideal. The index type Fin n is what the construction needs, because it uses the numerical distance j − i between indices. Mathlib has no corresponding coordinate-ring construction for unitriangular group schemes or their filtration stages, so there is no Mathlib counterpart.
